newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank says baht speculation over.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank says baht speculation over.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Friday that speculative attacks on the baht had ended and the situation for the embattled currency was returning to normal.

Deputy Bank of Thailand governor, Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi, also told a news conference that the central bank was ready to help ease liquidity if the interbank rate rose sharply on Friday as another measure to calm the money market.

"Since yesterday there has been no speculation (in the baht). If there is any speculation we will do our duty," he said. "Today liquidity will be tight. But the Bank of Thailand will ensure that those with liquidity problems will be helped."

Speculative attacks on the baht this week forced swap rates to soar, sparked heavy Thai and other regional central bank intervention to keep the currency from sliding and sent shockwaves through the Thai stock market.
However, on Friday, forex dealers said they noted selling of dollars for the baht in the spot market by those seeking to ease their tight baht liquidity.
The baht was quoted slightly weaker at 25.450/650 in the late morning against 25.300/340 late on Thursday. The central bank fixed the midrate at 25.82 versus the dollar.
